What you're hearing. The strip isn't an audio recording. Each line is a galvanometer trace from a Tucker hot-wire microphone, whose output was rectified (always one-sided), so it shows when and how hard pressure pulses arrived, not a sound wave. These sounds are built from those traced pulses. Audible fills each pulse with 25–180 Hz rumble so it carries on ordinary speakers. Strictly accurate keeps everything inside the microphones' response (resonance about 30–50 Hz, guns measured at 10–25 Hz) and needs headphones or a subwoofer. The meters show activity either way. Pitch up multiplies every frequency by a whole number (2×, 3×…) so small speakers that can't play deep bass can still carry the sound. Timing and loudness of each pulse are unchanged; only the pitch moves. 1× is the original. The soft chime marks where the strip was cut (about two minutes removed). Time scale: tick marks on the top line, 0.5 s apart. Mic 6 has faded out of the print after the cut, so it is silent there.
Source: frontispiece, America's Munitions 1917–1918, report of Benedict Crowell, Government Printing Office, 1919.
